description: Kentucky-only rules checked against the Kentucky Revised Statutes and 601 KAR 13:025. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: Unless a lower speed is required or the Transportation Cabinet sets a different limit, the speed limit on Kentucky interstate highways and parkways is
questions.explanation: KRS 189.390(3)(a) sets 65 mph on interstate highways and parkways. A 70 mph figure is not the statutory default.

questions.q: On a Kentucky state highway that is not an interstate or parkway and is not in a business or residential district, the statutory speed limit is
questions.explanation: KRS 189.390(3)(b) sets 55 mph on all other state highways. Subsection (3)(c) uses 35 mph in a business or residential district.

questions.q: In a Kentucky business or residential district, the statutory speed limit is
questions.explanation: KRS 189.390(3)(c) sets 35 mph in a business or residential district. The section defines both districts by highway frontage.

questions.q: The Kentucky secretary of transportation may raise a listed interstate or parkway segment to 70 mph
options: On any state highway after a city requests it
Only by official order, on the segments listed
On every two-lane road outside a city
questions.explanation: KRS 189.390(4)(a) says the secretary shall not increase a subsection (3) limit above 65 mph, except that listed interstate and parkway segments may be increased to 70 mph. The 70 figure is an authorized increase, not the statewide interstate limit.

questions.q: Where Kentucky school flasher lights are operating, the speed limit is
questions.explanation: KRS 189.336(3) says the speed limit on highways where school flasher lights are in operation is determined by the governmental unit that controls that highway. That unit shall erect signs notifying motorists of the speed limit. The statute does not set one statewide school-zone number.

questions.q: Kentucky prohibits operating or being in physical control of a motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more when the breath or blood sample is taken
options: Within two hours of stopping operation
At any time within eight hours
Only at the police station the next day
questions.explanation: KRS 189A.010(1)(a) uses 0.08 or more measured by a scientifically reliable test of breath or blood taken within two hours of cessation of operation or physical control.

questions.q: If the person is under 21, KRS 189A.010(1)(f) prohibits an alcohol concentration of
options: 0.02 or more, measured within two hours
questions.explanation: KRS 189A.010(1)(f) uses 0.02 or more for a person under 21, with the same two-hour breath or blood testing window as the adult 0.08 rule.

questions.q: In a Kentucky under-the-influence prosecution, an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or greater but less than 0.08
options: Is the commercial-vehicle per se offense
Is a presumption that the defendant was not under the influence
Creates no presumption, but may be weighed with other evidence
questions.explanation: KRS 189A.010(3)(b) says 0.04 or greater but less than 0.08 is not a presumption either way. A result under 0.04 is a presumption that the defendant was not under the influence.

questions.q: 601 KAR 13:025 lets the Transportation Cabinet suspend or probate the driving privilege of a driver age 18 or older who accumulates
options: 6 or more penalty points in two years
12 or more penalty points within two years
questions.explanation: Section 6 of 601 KAR 13:025 covers a person 18 or older who accumulates 12 or more penalty points within two years. A driver under 18 reaches that section at 7 or more penalty points within two years.

questions.q: For a driver under 18, 601 KAR 13:025 uses a two-year penalty-point total of
options: 12 points, the same as an adult
questions.explanation: Section 6(1)(b) applies to a person under 18 who accumulates seven or more penalty points within two years. Section 5 sends that driver a warning letter at four or more points.

questions.q: Under 601 KAR 13:025, speeding 16 mph or more but less than 26 mph over the limit is assessed
options: 0 points on a limited-access highway only
A mandatory 90-day suspension with no points
questions.explanation: Section 4(2) assigns six penalty points for speeding 16 mph or more but less than 26 mph over the limit. Speeding 15 mph or less is three points, with the KRS 186.572 exception. Speeding 26 mph or more is listed separately as a serious violation that may cause a 90-day suspension.

questions.q: A person who is at least 15 may apply for a Kentucky motor-vehicle instruction permit. While driving, the permit holder must be accompanied by a person with a valid operator's license who is
options: At least 18 and seated anywhere in the vehicle
At least 21 and occupying the seat beside the operator
questions.explanation: KRS 186.450(1) sets the application age at 15. Subsection (4)(b) requires a validly licensed person at least 21 in the seat beside the operator. A driver-training instructor supervising a multiple-vehicle range is the stated exception.

questions.q: An instruction-permit holder under 18 may not operate a motor vehicle, motorcycle, or moped between midnight and 6 a.m. unless
options: The trip is on an interstate
The person shows good cause, like work
The permit has been held for 30 days
questions.explanation: KRS 186.450(5) uses midnight to 6 a.m. and the good-cause showing, including but not limited to emergencies, school-related activities, or work-related activities.

questions.q: Before applying for an intermediate license, a Kentucky applicant who is 16 but under 18 must have held an instruction permit at least 180 days and must present a parent or guardian statement of at least
questions.explanation: KRS 186.452(1)(c) requires at least 60 hours of supervised driving, including at least 10 hours at night, with a licensed person at least 21 in the seat beside the applicant. The permit-holding period is 180 days under KRS 186.450(3)(b) and 186.452(1)(b).

questions.q: An intermediate licensee under 18 may not drive between midnight and 6 a.m. without good cause, and may not drive with more than one unrelated person under 20 unless
options: The extra passenger is a sibling of any age sitting in the back
A school-affiliated driver-training instructor accompanies the driver
The drive is shorter than 10 miles
The intermediate license is more than 30 days old
questions.explanation: KRS 186.452(4) and (5) state the midnight-to-6 a.m. rule and the one-unrelated-passenger-under-20 rule. The passenger rule does not apply when the named driver-training instructor accompanies the licensee, and it does not apply to a vehicle registered under KRS 186.050(4) while the operator is engaged in agricultural activities.

questions.q: In Kentucky, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Kentucky issues a learner's permit for a car at 15 years at the earliest.
questions.remember: Kentucky car permit: 15 years at the earliest.

provenance.manual: KRS 186.450 Instruction permits for motor vehicle and motorcycle

questions.q: In Kentucky, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Kentucky requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.

provenance.manual: KRS 186.450 Instruction permits for motor vehicle and motorcycle

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Kentucky complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Kentucky requires 60 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

provenance.manual: KRS 186.452 Intermediate license to operate a motor vehicle

questions.q: Of a Kentucky teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Kentucky requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.
questions.remember: Kentucky: 10 hours of the supervised driving at night.

provenance.manual: KRS 186.452 Intermediate license to operate a motor vehicle

questions.q: In Kentucky, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.

provenance.manual: KRS 186.452 Intermediate license to operate a motor vehicle

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in Kentucky not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: Kentucky restricts provisional drivers from Midnight to 6 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.
questions.remember: Kentucky new drivers: off the road Midnight to 6 a.m..

provenance.manual: KRS 186.452 Intermediate license to operate a motor vehicle

questions.q: In Kentucky, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Kentucky drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 17 years.

provenance.manual: KRS 186.454 Intermediate license holder application process

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Kentucky car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the Kentucky car knowledge test.

questions.q: In Kentucky, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.
questions.remember: Kentucky, 21 and over: 0.08% is over the limit.

provenance.manual: KRS 189A.010 Operating motor vehicle with alcohol concentration of or above 0.08

questions.q: In Kentucky, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: Kentucky sets the under-21 limit at 0.02%.

provenance.manual: KRS 189A.010 Operating motor vehicle with alcohol concentration of or above 0.08

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Kentucky?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Kentucky can be posted up to 70 mph for cars.
questions.remember: Kentucky rural interstate: up to 70 mph.

questions.q: Which best describes Kentucky's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Only texting is banned for all drivers
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
questions.explanation: Kentucky: only texting is banned for all drivers.

provenance.manual: KRS 189.292 Use of personal communication device prohibited while operating motor vehicle

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Kentucky?
options: Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.
questions.remember: Kentucky left on red: one-way onto one-way only.

questions.q: How is Kentucky's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
No seat belt law for adults
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
questions.explanation: Kentucky seat belt enforcement is primary.

provenance.manual: KRS 189.125 Requirements of use of seat belts, child restraint systems, and child booster seats

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Kentucky?
questions.explanation: Kentucky requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.
questions.remember: Kentucky: car or booster seat until 8 years.

provenance.manual: KRS 189.125 Requirements of use of seat belts, child restraint systems, and child booster seats

questions.q: What is Kentucky's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Kentucky requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $25,000.

provenance.manual: KRS 304.39-110 Required minimum tort liability insurance

questions.q: Under Kentucky's point system, what is the lowest point total that can suspend an adult's license?
questions.explanation: Kentucky can suspend an adult's license at 12 points in 24 months.
